To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HT-29 cells, which are a model of enterocytic cells, are a useful tool to study the posttranslational modifications of the sucrase-isomal-tase protein.

(1) the expression of sucrase isomaltase in differentiated cells is the result of both its synthesis and a slow degradation; (2) the expression of the enzyme in differentiated cells is not the result of its synthesis but rather of a slow degradation; and (3) the absence of sucrese isomaltase expression is not the result but the consequence of its rapid degradation.

the biosynthesis of sucrese-isomaltase (SIS) is not affected by the differentiation state of HT-29 cells, but that the posttranslational maturation of SIS is impaired in undifferentiated HT-29 cells and that the enzyme is rapidly degraded in this situation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the posttranslational events involved in the expression of the sucrase-isomal- tase enzyme in HT-29 human colonic adenocarcinoma cells.
the posttranslational maturation of sucrase- isomaltase in enterocyte-like HT-29 cells and its relationship to their state of differentiation.
the biosynthesis, the posttranslational modifications and the degradation of sucrase- isomaltase in undifferentiated and differentiated cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sucrase-isomalatase expression in HT-29 is a function of the enterocytic differentiation of the cells.

the expression of sucrase isomaltase is a function of the state of differentiation of the cells and that the absence of the enzyme in HT-29 cell lines grown in the presence (or absence) of glucose reflects the absence of a complete enterocytic differentiation in these cells.
the posttranslational maturation of sucrase isomaltase, as well as its expression, is a function of the enterocytic state of HT-29 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the posttranslational modifications of sucrase- isomaltase, which are necessary for its expression, are a function of the differentiation state of the cells and that this expression is regulated by glucose.
the biosynthesis and the post-translational processing of the sucrase-isomalatase are a function of the state of enterocitic differentiation of the HT-29 cells.
the biosynthesis and the posttranslational modifications of sucrase isomaltase in the HT-29 cells are a function of their enterocytic differentiation state and are regulated in a coordinated way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sucrase-isomalatase expression is not a simple reflection of the differentiation state of the cells.
sucrase-isomalatase is not synthesized in undifferentiated HT-29 cells, which may be a consequence of a lack of glycosylation and/or degradation of the enzyme.
sucrase-isomalatase is a good model for studying the role of the enterocyte differentiation state on the posttranslational maturation of a brush border enzyme.
